headline: Data-center surge and tariff refunds power a blowout quarter
summary_short: Generac's Q2 2026 net sales rose 10.6% y/y to $1.17B, with net income up 93.5% to $143.2M ($2.40 diluted EPS) as a roughly $71M pre-tax tariff refund lifted margins. The company raised FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20.0%-21.0% from 18.5%-19.5%.
summary_long: Net sales grew 10.6% y/y to $1.17B (C&I +29% on data-center ramp; Residential -2% on lower ESS/portable shipments). Gross margin expanded to 44.5% from 39.3%, aided ~6 points by a $71M pre-tax tariff-refund benefit, partly offset by unfavorable mix and higher input costs. Operating income rose 88.2% to $210.4M; net income rose 93.5% to $143.2M ($2.40 diluted EPS) versus $74.0M ($1.25) a year ago. Free cash flow roughly quadrupled to $62.9M. Cash was $264.9M and long-term debt $1.19B. Generac raised FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20.0%-21.0% (from 18.5%-19.5%) and net income margin guidance to 9.0%-10.0% (from 8.0%-9.0%).

drivers.explanation: C&I segment sales rose ~29% on ramping data-center demand and recently finalized hyperscale volume commitments; Residential fell ~2% on lower storage/portable shipments, partly offset by home standby growth.
Tariff refunds contributed ~6 points to gross margin; unfavorable sales mix and higher input costs were partly offset by favorable price realization.
Opex rose only 2% (higher C&I growth investment and intangible amortization, offset by lower legal costs) while gross profit jumped, driving the margin expansion.
Includes a ~$71M pre-tax tariff-refund benefit; the effective tax rate rose to 24.6% from 17.2% as a favorable one-time item in the prior-year quarter did not repeat.
Growth is consistent with retained-earnings accretion from six-month net income of $216.5M; unlike a year ago, the Company made no share repurchases in the current six-month period.

Management cited accelerating C&I/data-center momentum, a second hyperscale supply agreement signed in the quarter, and a $1.6B data-center-market backlog; the Enercon acquisition and Belvidere facility add megawatt-generator capacity.
